name: COHERENT
full_name: COHERENT experiment at the Spallation Neutron Source
summary: COHERENT is based at the Spallation Neutron Source, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Tennessee. Its multitarget program primarily studies coherent elastic neutrino–nucleus scattering, while actual data also constrain beam-produced light dark matter.
detection_principle: Proton collisions at a spallation-neutron-source target produce candidate particles; low-threshold detectors measure nuclear recoils. Beam timing and recoil spectra distinguish dark-matter scattering from coherent neutrino scattering.

results.summary: The CsI result found no dark-matter evidence and constrained quark couplings of a leptophobic vector portal.
Another CsI analysis probes model parameters of scalar dark matter at 1–220 MeV/c², reaching part of the expected thermal-relic region.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered.
